A 6-month-old male infant is brought to a well-child visit with concerns about persistent rightward head
turning. His mother reports attempting to correct this by repositioning his head during sleep, without

success. She is uncertain about the onset timing. The infant experienced a fall from bed the previous
day but was easily consoled. He is meeting developmental milestones, including solid food
introduction, babbling, and sitting with support. Birth history includes cesarean delivery at 37 weeks for
breech presentation. Vital signs show: temperature 99.1°F (37°C), blood pressure 84/50 mmHg, pulse
119/min, and respirations 21/min. Physical examination reveals right head turn with left head tilt, minor
bruising on the posterior head and sternocleidomastoid muscle. Vision appears normal with
appropriate focusing ability. What is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices:
(A) Reassurance and follow-up in one month (B) Cranial ultrasound (C) Observation and reassessment
in two weeks (D) CT scan of the head (E) MRI of the cervical spine (F) Trial of neck stretching
exercises (G) Neck radiograph (H) Ophthalmology referral (I) Referral to physical therapy (J) Referral
to a pediatric neurologist
 A. Cranial ultrasound
